children: Bank Nifty fell as much as 0.7 percent on September 1, giving back a large part of the sharp Closing Auction Session (CAS)-driven jump seen in the previous session, even as the broader market traded higher. The banking index was trading down 0.7 percent at 57,625 around 12:05 pm, nearly 400 points below its previous close of 58,025. It had slipped as low as 57,317 during the session, a decline of more than 700 points from Monday's closing level.

The reversal comes after an unusual finish to the August 31 session, when Bank Nifty surged more than 600 points during the closing auction alone. The index was at 57,397 around 3:15 pm but finished at 58,025 after CAS, ending the day 529 points, or 0.92 percent, higher.

Tuesday's decline therefore took Bank Nifty back towards levels prevailing before Monday's closing-auction spike. At its intraday low of 57,316.60, the index had fallen below its 3:15 pm level from the previous session.

The weakness in banks also stood in contrast to the headline indices. At 12:05 pm, the Sensex was up 250 points, or 0.33 percent, at 77,207, while the Nifty gained 45 points to 24,125. Market breadth was almost evenly split, with 1,853 shares advancing against 1,904 declines.

The weakness was broad-based across banking stocks. Yes Bank fell nearly 3 percent, while Axis Bank declined more than 2 percent. IndusInd Bank, Federal Bank and SBI lost between 1.7 percent and 1.9 percent, while ICICI Bank and IDFC First Bank were down more than 1 percent each. Kotak Mahindra Bank bucked the trend, rising nearly 2 percent, while PNB gained more than 1 percent. HDFC Bank and Bank of Baroda were marginally higher.
Other banking indices were also in the red, with the Nifty PSU Bank down 0.64 percent and the Nifty Private Bank declining 0.50 percent.

Monday's outsized CAS move came on the first MSCI index-rebalancing day since the closing-auction mechanism was introduced. NSE recorded Rs 39,718 crore of turnover during the August 31 CAS, around 42 times the previous trading day's level and accounting for 22 percent of the exchange's total cash-market turnover for the day.

The Closing Auction Session, introduced by the NSE in August, is a separate 20-minute mechanism used to determine the official closing prices of eligible stocks. It replaced the earlier system under which closing prices were calculated using the weighted average of trades during the final half-hour of continuous trading.

The reversal is also notable in light of Monday's technical commentary. Vatsal Bhuva, technical analyst at LKP Securities, had said after the close that follow-up buying would be necessary to confirm the sustainability of Bank Nifty's breakout attempt because much of the surge had occurred during CAS. He had identified immediate resistance at 58,200 and support at 57,300. Tuesday's intraday low of 57,316.6 brought the index almost exactly to that support zone.

title: Bank Nifty falls 400 points today as CAS-driven surge fizzles out; Axis Bank, Yes Bank lead losses
